MICRO.description: Fastest track for trivial fixes: you already know the file and the change. No discovery, no subagents, no review. Just fix, verify, commit.

steps.name: intake
checklist: Confirm the bug and expected fix with user in 1-2 sentences
Create requirement.md with a one-liner description
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
steps.adaptive: Skip all questions if the user's start command already has enough context. Just confirm and proceed.

steps.name: code
checklist: Read the relevant file(s) — use grep + view_file directly (no subagent)
Make the fix
Write a brief context.md with ## Hypothesis and ## Fix sections
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: commit
checklist: Stage changed files: `git add {files}`
Commit: `git commit -m "fix({module}): {summary} Ref: {TASK_ID}"`
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py done --force`

EXPRESS.description: Fast track for simple bugs: recipe found, single module, obvious fix.

steps.name: intake
checklist: Review what the user already provided (URL, expected, actual, steps) in requirement.md
For MISSING fields only — ask the user. Skip questions already answered.

Bug fix questions: Which screen/URL? What is the expected value vs actual value? Steps to reproduce? Specific record ID or date range to test with? Does this bug happen for all records or just specific ones?
Feature/CR questions: Who requested? User story? Acceptance criteria? Existing similar feature? New DB tables needed?
Update requirement.md with answers — fill in ## Description, ## Current Behavior, ## Expected Behavior
If ALL context is already clear from start command flags: just confirm with user and proceed
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
forbidden: Do NOT read source code — no grep, no view_file on controllers/models
Do NOT investigate the bug — just gather context
steps.adaptive: If --url, --expected, --actual, --steps were all provided at start, summarize what you have and ask: 'Anything else to add, or shall I proceed?' — don't interrogate.

steps.name: discover
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py discover`
Wait for completion (do NOT run other commands in parallel)
Confirm: discovery.md was created (check console output)
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
forbidden: Do NOT read brain docs manually — discover does this
Do NOT grep source code — discover does this
Do NOT kill the discover command — it handles timeouts internally
steps.on_failure: STOP. Report what failed to user. Ask: 'Approve manual investigation?' Wait for response.

steps.name: code
checklist: Read discovery.md — note the call tree, code excerpts, and file paths with line numbers
Read the specific source files at the line ranges identified by discovery (do NOT read entire files)
Identify root cause — which line(s) are wrong and why
Make the minimum fix. Run `php -l {file}` to syntax check each changed file
Write context.md with ## Hypothesis and ## Fix sections
Write test_cases.md with minimum 3 test cases (fix verification, edge case, regression)
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: verify
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a subagent with the prompt (agent_type: self)
Wait for subagent to complete
Validate: context.md has ## Verification section
Validate: Overall Verdict is PASS
If FAIL: report to user, ask for next action
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: commit
checklist: Stage changed files: `git add {files}`
Generate rollback plan in context.md ## Rollback section: `git revert {commit_hash}`, affected files list, test to verify rollback
Commit: `git commit -m "fix({module}): {summary} Ref: {TASK_ID}"`
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py enrich`
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py done`

Feature/CR questions: Who requested? User story? Acceptance criteria? Existing similar feature? New DB tables needed?
Update requirement.md with answers — fill in ## Description, ## Current Behavior, ## Expected Behavior
If ALL context is already clear from start command flags: just confirm with user and proceed
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

Do NOT investigate the bug — just gather context
steps.adaptive: If --url, --expected, --actual, --steps were all provided at start, summarize what you have and ask: 'Anything else to add, or shall I proceed?' — don't interrogate.

steps.name: discover
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py discover`
Wait for completion (do NOT run other commands in parallel)
Confirm: discovery.md was created (check console output)
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
forbidden: Do NOT read brain docs manually — discover does this
Do NOT search recipes manually — discover does this
Do NOT grep source code — discover does this
Do NOT kill the discover command — it handles timeouts internally
steps.on_failure: STOP. Report what failed to user. Ask: 'Approve manual investigation?' Wait for response.

steps.name: investigate
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a RESEARCH subagent with the prompt
Wait for subagent to complete
Validate: context.md exists in task directory with ## Hypothesis section
If insufficient: send follow-up message to subagent with specific questions
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
forbidden: Do NOT read source code yourself — delegate to subagent
Do NOT investigate the bug yourself
steps.fallback: If subagent fails completely: kill it, report to user, ask 'Approve manual investigation?'

steps.name: test_design
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a RESEARCH subagent with the prompt
Wait for subagent to complete
Validate: test_cases.md exists with minimum 3 test cases
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: plan
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a SELF subagent with the prompt
Wait for subagent to complete
Validate: requirement_review.md artifact was created
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: review
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a RESEARCH subagent with the prompt
Wait for subagent to complete
Read review.md in the task directory
If verdict is REJECT: send review feedback back to a NEW plan subagent (re-run step 5 logic), then re-run this review step
If verdict is CONCERNS: append the concerns to the requirement_review.md artifact before presenting to user
If verdict is PASS: proceed to approval
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
forbidden: Do NOT skip the review even if the plan looks good
Do NOT present the plan to the user before review completes
steps.on_reject: Re-run plan step with review feedback. Max 2 revision cycles before escalating to user.

steps.name: approval
checklist: Present the fix plan (requirement_review.md) to user — include review verdict and any concerns
WAIT for user to approve the plan
When user approves: copy approved plan to .sdlc/active/{TASK_ID}/requirement.md
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: code
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a SELF subagent with the prompt
Wait for subagent to complete
Validate: git has uncommitted changes (the fix)
Validate: test file exists in tests/tests/
Validate: test_cases.md has ## Generated Tests section
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`
forbidden: Do NOT write code yourself — delegate to subagent

steps.name: verify
checklist: Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py get-prompt` to get the subagent prompt
Spawn a SELF subagent with the prompt
Wait for subagent to complete
Validate: context.md has ## Verification section with Overall Verdict
If Overall Verdict is FAIL: report to user, ask for next action — do NOT proceed
If Overall Verdict is PASS: proceed
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py step-done`

steps.name: commit
checklist: Stage changed files: `git add {files}`
Generate rollback plan in context.md ## Rollback section: `git revert {commit_hash}`, affected files list, test to verify rollback
Commit: `git commit -m "fix({module}): {summary} Ref: {TASK_ID}"`
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py enrich` — generates recipe from all task artifacts
Push recipe to central repo: read the generated recipe .md file, then call GitHub MCP create_or_update_file (owner: LOGIMAX-CLIENTS, repo: bug-recipes, path: recipes/{module}/{recipe_id}.md)
Run: `python .sdlc/engine/cli.py done`
